title: KnowledgeSmith: Uncovering Knowledge Updating in LLMs with Model Editing and Unlearning
claim: A static knowledge source is turned into leveled probes and a benchmark, then used to compare editing and unlearning under one objective.
layout: 3 stacked panels, top-to-bottom, big arrows between, loss equation in bottom panel
description: Three rounded, color-coded panels are stacked vertically and linked by large downward arrows. The top blue panel, 'Subjects & Knowledge Graph', lists subject icons (Biology, Economics, History, Physics) beside a three-level tree. Root, intermediate and leaf questions about the DNA double helix sit to the right of the tree. The middle peach panel, 'Automatic Benchmark Generation', is a left-to-right chain of four steps joined by hollow arrows: entity-relation selection, template-based question generation, multiple-choice generation and external validation. The bottom green panel, 'KnowledgeSmith', opens with a constrained-optimization loss equation. Below it, two mirrored flows show Knowledge Editing (localized update) and Machine Unlearning (distributed update). Each flow takes an original LLM and a post-modified LLM through the same question to an answer: 1953 marked wrong with a red cross, 1955 marked correct with a green check. The eye goes first to the top title tab and then down the stack.
caption: \method pipeline. Starting from static KG, we generate dynamic probes at root, intermediate, and leaf levels, enabling evaluation of direct and propagated effects.
abstract: Knowledge editing and machine unlearning are two popular approaches for large language models (LLMs) to stay up-to-date. However, the knowledge updating mechanism of LLMs remains largely unexplored due to insufficient, isolated, and small-scale evaluation. For instance, are LLMs similar to humans in modifying certain knowledge? What differs editing and unlearning as training data increases? This paper proposes KnowledgeSmith, a unified framework to systematically understand the updating mechanism of LLMs. We first cast editing and unlearning as instances of one constrained optimization problem. Then, we propose an automatic dataset generator that provides structured interventions across multiple graph levels and data scales, enabling controlled studies of how different modification strategies propagate through model knowledge. Extensive experiments demonstrate nuanced insights over knowledge propagation, plasticity scaling, consistency, and robustness. For instance, our results show that LLMs do not exhibit similar updating as humans for different levels of knowledge, and there exists consistency-capacity trade-off. We hope our findings can offer suggestions to the design of more reliable and scalable strategies. Code: https://github.com/AIFrontierLab/KnowledgeSmith.git
